lines.cap: Early golf balls were smooth. And golfers noticed something strange.
lines.say: Early golf balls were smooth. And golfers noticed something strange.

lines.cap: Old, beaten up balls, full of dents and scratches, flew further than new ones.
lines.say: Old, beaten up balls, full of dents and scratches, flew further than new ones.

lines.cap: Here's why. Air flowing over a smooth ball peels away early, leaving a big pocket of drag behind it.
lines.say: Here's why. Air flowing over a smooth ball peels away early, leaving a big pocket of drag behind it.

lines.cap: Dimples make a thin layer of air cling to the ball for longer. The pocket behind it shrinks.
lines.say: Dimples make a thin layer of air cling to the ball for longer. The pocket behind it shrinks.

lines.cap: Less drag. And with backspin, more lift. A dimpled ball can fly about twice as far.
lines.say: Less drag. And with backspin, more lift. A dimpled ball can fly about twice as far.

lines.cap: Most golf balls have between three hundred and five hundred dimples.
lines.say: Most golf balls have between three hundred and five hundred dimples.

lines.cap: So size isn't everything. It's the dimples.
lines.say: So size isn't everything. It's the dimples.
